A.summary: Complete, through-via 6-layer board with solid In1/In4 ground planes, DDR3 matched to about 15.0 mm, a coupled 30 mm USB pair, pours for every rail and all FPGA decoupling under the BGA. Faults are housekeeping DRC items (zone edge 0.15 mm, NPTH clearance, a duplicate zone, 5 dangling vias) and very tight 0201 spacing (68 courtyard overlaps).

B.summary: Electrically complete and DRC-clean, but it needs an HDI build (197 microvias, 30 buried vias, custom stackup) rather than a standard 6-layer order, and VBUS/VBATT/VSYS are routed at 0.105 mm. Ground planes are perforated under the BGAs (97.6 mm2 void network on In1), DDR3 is unmatched with up to 6 vias per net, and the flash, ADC parts and SD filter are 15-23 mm from where they belong.

C.summary: Unfinished: 114 of 170 nets incomplete (210 unconnected items, 1252 mm of ratsnest), no rail delivered, USB, SD and the DDR clock unrouted. Bypass caps are parked in rows 4-8 mm from the FPGA and 0201 pads are placed on top of header and microSD pads.

D.summary: Sound stack-up (In2 stripline between two ground planes), correct power widths and good decoupling on a standard through-via process, but 27 unconnected items make it dead as drawn: the 2.5 V LDO output reaches no FPGA VCCAUX ball and 9 of 12 P1.35V FPGA balls are cut off from the regulator. B.Cu signals run over split power only, and the button, charge LED and ADC mux have open pins.

human_guess.why: A has DDR3 nets tuned to a target length with serpentines (24 address/control nets within 0.22 mm of 15.0 mm), 20 small hand-drawn regulator pours with individual priorities and ten rail islands on In3. Only J3 and J5 are locked in A, while B, C and D share the 19 locked footprints the job describes, so A did not start from the stripped job file. Its violations are legacy-style (dense courtyard overlaps, fills a few microns under a rule), whereas the other three show regular placement grids, parked capacitor rows, incomplete nets or HDI vias used to escape congestion.
